items.title: OpenAI CFO questions Altman's push for late 2026 IPO

featured_image.name: OpenAI hires former Nextdoor CEO Sarah Friar as first CFO ...

items.description:
A rift has emerged at the top of OpenAI over the timing and affordability of what could become one of the largest public listings in technology history. Chief Financial Officer Sarah Friar has privately questioned CEO Sam Altman's push to take the company public as early as the fourth quarter of 2026, warning that OpenAI may not be organizationally prepared for such a move, according to a report by The Information published Saturday.[1]

Friar has also raised concerns about Altman's commitment to spend $600 billion on computing infrastructure over the next five years, citing doubts about whether the company's revenue trajectory can support purchases of that magnitude. The tensions between the two most senior figures overseeing OpenAI's finances and strategy represent an unusual public signal of internal friction at the world's most valuable startup.[2][3]

items.title: Chinese scientist reveals military uses for space solar project

featured_image.name: China looks set to build space solar power station-Xinhua

items.description: A senior Chinese scientist behind Beijing's ambitious space-based solar power program has published a paper outlining how the technology could be adapted for military operations, including surveillance, electronic warfare, and communications control, offering a rare public acknowledgment of the dual-use potential of one of China's most prominent energy megaprojects.

items.title: Study of 1,700 languages finds shared grammar rules

featured_image.name: Study of 1,700 languages reveals surprising hidden patterns | ScienceDaily

items.description: Despite the staggering diversity of the world's languages, many follow the same grammatical playbook. A large-scale study analyzing more than 1,700 languages has found that roughly one-third of long-proposed "linguistic universals" hold up under rigorous statistical testing, pointing to deep cognitive and communicative forces that shape how humans build language.[1][2]

items.title: Artemis II crew set to fly around the Moon on Monday

featured_image.name: NASA: Artemis II Crew

items.description:
Saudi Arabia has become the first Arab nation to participate in NASA's Artemis program after its domestically built Shams satellite was successfully deployed aboard the Space Launch System rocket as part of the Artemis II mission, the Saudi Space Agency confirmed over the weekend.[1][2]

The satellite, formally designated Space Weather CubeSat-1 in NASA documentation, is a 12U CubeSat that hitched a ride as a secondary payload when Artemis II lifted off from Kennedy Space Center on April 1. The Saudi Space Agency announced initial contact with the satellite on April 3, revealing its Arabic name — Shams, meaning "sun" — and outlining its scientific objectives.[3][4][5]

items.title: Iran accuses IAEA of inaction over Bushehr strikes

featured_image.name: Why an attack on Bushehr nuclear plant would be catastrophic for ...

items.description:
A projectile strike hit near Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant on Saturday, killing a security guard and damaging an auxiliary building in what marked the fourth attack on the facility since the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran began on February 28, the International Atomic Energy Agency confirmed.[1][2]

IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi expressed "deep concern" over the incident, stressing that "nuclear power plant sites or nearby areas must never be attacked" and warning that auxiliary buildings "may contain vital safety equipment". The agency reported no increase in radiation levels at the site.[2][1]

items.title: Artemis II crew flies past the moon in historic flyby

featured_image.name: Artemis II hits ‘two thirds’ mark on moon journey, shares new lunar photos: ‘History in the making’

items.description: As four astronauts sweep around the far side of the Moon on Monday, the historic Artemis II mission reaches its climax under the watch of two key figures on the ground: chief flight director Emily Nelson and mission manager Matthew Ramsey. The mission, which launched on April 1 from Kennedy Space Center, marks the first time humans have traveled to the Moon since Apollo 17 in 1972.[1][2]

items.title: IRGC intelligence chief killed in US-Israeli strikes that left at least 34 dead

featured_image.name: Majid Khademi appointed new IRGC intel chief | Al Mayadeen ...

items.description: Coordinated airstrikes by the United States and Israel killed at least 34 people across Iran on Monday, the 38th day of the war, in attacks that struck Tehran, Qom, and the southern port city of Bandar-e Lengeh. Among the dead was Major General Seyed Majid Khademi, the head of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' intelligence organization, according to an official IRGC statement carried by Iran's Fars news agency.[1][2]

items.title: Pakistan brokers ceasefire plan as Trump's Iran deadline nears Tuesday

featured_image.name: Pakistan emerges as key mediator to end US-Israel war on ...

items.description: The United States, Iran, and a group of regional mediators are racing to finalize terms for a potential 45-day ceasefire aimed at preventing a dramatic escalation of the war, as President Donald Trump's latest ultimatum for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approaches Tuesday evening.

items.title: Physicists cool nanorotor to quantum ground state in two dimensions

featured_image.name: Ground-state cooling of a nanoparticle along two directions ...

items.description: A team of European physicists has cooled the rotational motion of a levitated silica nanorotor to its quantum ground state in two dimensions for the first time, a result that opens new paths for quantum sensing and tests of fundamental physics. The work, published in Nature Physics on April 6, represents a leap beyond previous experiments that managed the feat in only one rotational axis.[1][2]

items.title: Study: 84% of fire-vulnerable species face rising wildfire risk by 2100

featured_image.name: Experts reveal climate change drove extreme wildfire seasons across the  Americas, making burned areas much larger

items.description: Climate-driven wildfires will place nearly 84 percent of fire-vulnerable species at heightened risk by 2100, according to a study published in Nature Climate Change on April 5. The research, led by Xiaoye Yang of the University of Gothenburg, offers one of the most comprehensive assessments to date of how shifting wildfire regimes could reshape threats to global biodiversity.[1]

items.title: Trump's deadline for Iran to reopen Strait of Hormuz arrives Monday

featured_image.name: Trump extends deadline for Iran to reopen oil route or face ... - PBS

items.description:
Global oil prices climbed again over the weekend, with U.S. crude rising above $114 per barrel and Brent crude topping $110, after President Donald Trump issued an expletive-laden ultimatum demanding Iran reopen the Strait of Hormuz by the end of Monday or face strikes on its civilian infrastructure.[1][2]

The latest price spike comes as the U.S.-Iran conflict enters its sixth week with no resolution in sight, and as Trump's self-imposed April 6 deadline for Iran to restore access to the critical waterway arrives.[3][4]

items.title: Artemis II crew begins historic lunar flyby Monday

featured_image.name: Meet the 4 astronauts flying on NASA's Artemis 2 moon mission | Space

items.description: Four astronauts aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft are poised to sweep around the Moon on Monday, capping a five-day outbound journey and marking the first time humans have traveled to the lunar neighborhood since Apollo 17 in 1972. The Artemis II crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, and Mission Specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen of the Canadian Space Agency — launched from Kennedy Space Center's Launch Complex 39B on April 1 at 6:35 p.m. EDT aboard the Space Launch System rocket.[1][2]

items.title: Iran hits Gulf infrastructure as Trump's 48-hour deadline nears

featured_image.name: Drone sparks fire at UAE oil site as Gulf takes more hits amid Iran war

items.description: Iran launched a new wave of missiles and drones at Gulf countries early Sunday, striking infrastructure across the UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, and Saudi Arabia as the conflict that began on February 28 entered its sixth week. The attacks came one day after President Donald Trump issued a 48-hour ultimatum for Tehran to reach a deal or face intensified strikes.[1]

items.title: IRGC says Hormuz will 'never return' as Trump deadline looms

featured_image.name: Trump gives Iran 48-hour deadline to reopen Strait of Hormuz or ...

items.description: Iran allowed 15 ships to transit the Strait of Hormuz over the past 24 hours under its permission-based corridor system, even as President Donald Trump set a Tuesday deadline threatening to strike Iranian power plants and bridges if the waterway is not fully reopened. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy declared Sunday that the strait will "never return to its former state, especially for the US and Israel," signaling Tehran's intent to permanently reshape control over one of the world's most critical maritime chokepoints.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Koch becomes farthest-traveling woman as Artemis II nears moon

featured_image.name: Get to know Christina Koch, the 1st female NASA astronaut to travel ...

items.description:
NASA astronaut Christina Koch has officially become the woman who has traveled the farthest from Earth, surpassing the distance records of every female astronaut before her as the Artemis II mission hurtles toward a lunar flyby scheduled for Monday.

Koch, 47, is one of four crew members aboard the Orion spacecraft — named Integrity — which launched from Kennedy Space Center on April 1 at 6:35 p.m. EDT. She passed the milestone on approximately April 3 as Orion left Earth orbit and entered its trans-lunar trajectory, moving well beyond the roughly 250-mile altitude of the International Space Station where all previous female astronauts had flown.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Gulf funds near $24B deal to back Paramount's Warner takeover

featured_image.name: Exclusive | Gulf Funds Near Deal to Back Paramount's $81 ...

items.description:
Paramount Skydance is nearing a $24 billion equity commitments from three Gulf sovereign wealth funds to finance its $81 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, in a move that would resolve weeks of uncertainty over whether Middle Eastern capital would remain part of the deal.[1][2][3]

Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund is contributing approximately $10 billion, the largest individual commitment, alongside investments from the Qatar Investment Authority and Abu Dhabi-based L'imad Holding Co., according to the report. The Gulf investors will hold minority, non-voting stakes, and Paramount does not expect the arrangement to trigger review by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States.[4][3]

items.title: Iran allows 15 ships through Hormuz in highest daily count since blockade

featured_image.name: Strait of Hormuz crisis explained: What it means for global shipping

items.description: Iran permitted 15 vessels to transit the Strait of Hormuz over the past 24 hours after granting them official clearance, according to Iran's semi-official Fars News Agency, as reported by The Wall Street Journal on Sunday. The uptick marks the highest single-day count since Tehran imposed a selective blockade on the strategic waterway in mid-March, though maritime traffic remains a fraction of normal volumes.[1][2]

items.title: Trump says NATO appeal on Hormuz was a deliberate 'test'

featured_image.name: If There's No Deal 'We're Blowing Up the Whole Country' - Yahoo

items.description:
President Donald Trump told ABC News that his appeals for NATO allies to help patrol the Strait of Hormuz were never a genuine request but rather a deliberate test of the alliance's resolve — one he says it failed.

"This was a test for NATO, I didn't need them, but I wanted to test them," Trump said in an interview with ABC News correspondent Rachel Scott published Sunday. "They're a paper tiger. Paper Tiger. They have no ships. They have nothing, and Putin has zero fear of them. But I did it as a test."[1][2]

The remarks are the latest in weeks of escalating rhetoric from Trump against the transatlantic defense pact, which he has criticized for refusing to join U.S. military operations against Iran. Trump first told Britain's Telegraph in an interview published April 1 that leaving NATO was "beyond reconsideration," calling allies "cowards" for declining to help reopen the strategic waterway.[3][4]

items.title: Study finds first evidence of 'forbidden' black hole mass gap

featured_image.name: Strange supernova blasts hint we have glimpsed a black ...

items.description: A trio of recent discoveries is reshaping how astronomers understand the violent ends of stars, from the heaviest stellar explosions ever theorized to aging suns that devour their own worlds and dead stars with puzzling split personalities.

items.title: Artemis II crew tests survival suits as Moon flyby nears

featured_image.name: NASA Answers Your Most Pressing Artemis II Questions

items.description: The four astronauts of NASA's Artemis II mission spent their fifth day in space Sunday testing the orange Orion Crew Survival System suits they would depend on in an emergency, as the spacecraft closed within roughly 60,000 miles of the Moon ahead of a historic flyby set for Monday afternoon.
